title: 66 Volunteers at the Dublin City Marathon 2025
excerpt: Sixty-six volunteers, parents, Scouts, Senior Cubs and Leaders, operated the 22-mile water station on Fosters Avenue from 7am through to the final walkers.
body:
It was an early start for our sixty six (66) volunteers including Parents, Scouts, Senior Cubs and Leaders, who all gathered at the Dunboyne Scout Den from 7am, ahead of what was sure to be a long day operating the 22 Mile Water Station located on Fosters Avenue, just after the infamous Heartbreak Hill on Roebuck Road.

Being stationed on the second to last water station on the 26 mile course, ensured it would be a long day for all who volunteered. However our group was very much up for the marathon shift that would be needed, to take us through from initial water station setup on Fosters Avenue from before 8am, right through until after the last of the walkers made their way past the water station, and all rubbish and debris had been cleared up. #LeaveNoTrace

Even though the weather was somewhat inclement throughout the day, there was a great spirit of camaraderie between our volunteers. All who participated did our group proud and represented the very best of 1st Meath Dunboyne Scout Group and contributed to the smooth running of yet another highly successful Dublin City Marathon for 2025.

Bravo to all who volunteered their time & effort on a damp bank holiday Sunday!!

title: Ventures at Kandersteg International Scout Camp, Switzerland
excerpt: Our Ventures spent a week at KISC in the Swiss Alps, hiking to 2,840m, white-water rafting Grade IV rapids, and meeting Scouts from Australia, Sweden, the USA and Scotland.
body:
Our Ventures headed to Kandersteg International Scout Camp (KISC) in the Swiss Alps for an unforgettable week of adventure. The camp is a 100+ year-old facility that hosted Baden Powell's first World Scout Moot, and it showed, scouts from Australia, Sweden, USA and Scotland were among those sharing the site.

The week kicked off with gondola access to the Rodelbahn mountain toboggan run, followed by a swim in the Oeschinen glacial lake. When weather forced a change of plan mid-week, the group headed to Thun to explore the castle and watch daredevils river-surfing the Aare. The evening campfire featured skits and songs with international groups.

The highlight was an eight-hour alpine hike to the Blüemlisalp Hut at 2,840m elevation, epic views across the mountain peaks and paragliders launching from the ridge. The group were up again at 5:30am the next morning to watch the alpine sunrise before a snowman-building session and more lake swimming.

The final adventure day in Interlaken brought high ropes courses and white-water rafting on Grade III and IV rapids on the Lütschine River. An incredible week clocking up roughly 20,000 steps a day, well done to all who took part!

title: Beaver Summer Camp 2025, Collon, Co. Louth
excerpt: 34 Beavers, parents and leaders headed to Collon Scout Camp for a weekend of swing-building, bridge-building, a visit to the Irish Military Museum, and mandatory s'mores.
body:
The weekend of June 20–22 brought together the entire Beaver troop for their summer camp at Collon Scout Camp Site in County Louth. Parents, Beavers and Leaders gathered at Dunboyne Scout Den on Friday afternoon to load the bus, tents, cooking equipment, tables, chairs, benches, first aid kits, pioneering spars, and games all packed, and departed at 17:20, ten minutes ahead of schedule.

Friday evening was all about settling in: tents up, flag raised, Beavers allocated to accommodations, and mandatory s'mores before bed.

Saturday was the big day. Three rotating morning stations kept everyone busy: Camp Games, Swing Building, and Bridge Building. By the end of the morning the Beavers had constructed a complete playground, a swing set, volleyball court, tree swings and a rope bridge, which they spent the rest of camp testing to destruction.

The afternoon brought an extensive guided tour of the Irish Military Museum, with archery, a World War I rifle demonstration and talk from staff, and souvenirs to bring home. Saturday ended around a campfire with songs the Beavers have been learning all year.

Special thanks to camp chiefs Martha, Celine, and Matt for feeding everyone brilliantly throughout the weekend. Sunday brought the closing ceremony, where each Beaver was presented with a commemorative camp badge, torch and compass. A brilliant weekend!

title: Velociraptor Patrol Earns Silver at National Phoenix Competition
excerpt: The Velociraptor Patrol represented Gleann na Boinne and 1st Meath Dunboyne at the all-Ireland Phoenix competition in Limerick, earning a Silver Standard in backwoods, pioneering and team challenges.
body:
The Velociraptor Patrol travelled to Limerick to represent Gleann na Boinne, and 1st Meath Dunboyne, at the National Phoenix Competition, the all-Ireland Scout skills championship with 400–500 Scouts competing.

The patrol demonstrated their abilities across backwoods camping, pioneering construction, and team challenge events over what the group described as “a magnificent weekend of super memories.”

The team earned a Silver Standard, a fantastic result at national level. Huge credit to mentors Barry and Tony, and to the Scout Leaders, for the preparation that went into this performance.

BRAVO..!!

title: Water Section Shines at the Boyne Descent 2025
excerpt: Over 20 Scout groups and nearly 90 paddlers on the Trim to Bective route, Alex Betson took 2nd in the U16 category, James Sludds 3rd in the Rover & Leader category.
body:
Our Water Section took to the River Boyne for the annual Boyne Descent, competing on the Trim to Bective route alongside over 20 Scout groups and nearly 90 participants.

It was a brilliant day on the water, with two standout individual results for 1st Meath Dunboyne: Alex Betson secured 2nd place in the Under 16 category, and James Sludds earned 3rd place in the Rover & Leader category.

Well done to all who participated, and to everyone in the Water Section who trains week in, week out to make performances like this possible. The Boyne Descent is one of the highlights of the scouting calendar and this year was no exception.

Well done to all…!!!!

title: Monday Beavers Navigate Carton House by Night
excerpt: The Monday Beaver section practised map and compass navigation across the Carton House estate, finding the Boathouse, following the Rye River, and reaching Tyrconnell Tower.
body:
The Monday Beavers were out in force at the beautiful Carton House estate for a navigation and hiking evening, practising real map and compass skills across the grounds.

Working in pairs, the buddy system very much in play, the Beavers followed their maps to find three key landmarks: the Boathouse by the water, the Rye River path, and the Tyrconnell Tower as their final destination.

The activity focused on safe hiking techniques, teamwork and responsibility, and developing a love for exploring, and by all accounts the Beavers absolutely loved it. A great evening out for the whole section!

title: Scout Team Win Gleann na Boinne County Shield Final
excerpt: First place in the Gleann na Boinne County Shield, pioneering, backwoods, and amazing team spirit earn the Scouts a place at the Phoenix all-Ireland competition.
body:
The Scout Team from 1st Meath Dunboyne have done it, first place in the Gleann na Boinne County Shield Final!

The team demonstrated their skills in Pioneering and Backwoods and showed amazing team spirit throughout the competition. The result earns them a place at the Phoenix, the all-Ireland competition with 400–500 Scouts competing from across the country.

Huge thanks and recognition to mentors Barry and Tony, and to the Scout Leaders, for all the preparation and support that went into this win.

title: Darkness Into Light 2025, Scouts Support Pieta at Fairyhouse
excerpt: 25 volunteers from Cubs, Scouts, Ventures, Leaders and Parents supported Darkness Into Light at Fairyhouse Racecourse, a 2:30am start and over 1,000 participants crossing the finish by sunrise.
body:
On May 10th, representatives from Cubs, Scouts and Ventures along with Leaders and Parents, 25 in total, gathered in the early hours to volunteer at the Darkness Into Light event at Fairyhouse Racecourse.

With a 2:30am start, it was no easy task. But the group was fully committed to supporting an event that highlights a hugely important topic. As the sun rose above the track at 5:30am, over 1,000 participants completed the 5km course and made their way home.

The faces on people, the conversations heard, the smiles, the tears, it was a form of healing and acknowledgement that our volunteers were proud to be part of. Our scout volunteers thoroughly enjoyed the morning and all have signed up again for 2026!
